# B5-M grading calibration

These are four constructed grading controls, not subject executions. They are excluded from the 42-trial performance denominator. The control answers and expected requirement statuses are fixed before either semantic assessment begins; later grades must not be used to revise them.

Only B5-M's original task/source and eight fixed criteria, plus the authorized assessment-status instructions, informed this set. No subject output, method file, execution history, trial mapping, earlier judgment or study conclusion informed the controls.

G01 is a decision memo with a table. G02 is a continuous explanatory note with arithmetic written out. Both meet all eight criteria; their different wording and organization are intentionally immaterial. G03 contains favorable-only success aggregation, deliberate exclusion of the regression, unsupported conversion of executor seconds into billing credits, and a population-quality release overclaim. G04 contains model/timeout confounding, both reversed substantive grader labels, an exposed-set-as-holdout error, rejection of the needed follow-up, and a cross-model release overclaim.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| B5-M-1 | met | met | refuted | met |
| B5-M-2 | met | met | refuted | met |

Each expected status in calibration.json includes criterion-specific source and answer evidence. A concrete contradiction or omission is refuted. The correct subparts of a compound criterion do not cancel a concrete violation: G03 has correct executor sums but still refutes criterion 3 by converting them into actual billed costs without source support. The roundings 66.7% and +16.7 percentage points represent the exact sixths in S1.

Start with the six pairs in S1. Without Z the success sum is 1+0+1+0+1+0 = 3; with Z it is 1+1+0+0+1+1 = 4. Thus 3/6 (50%) becomes 4/6 (about 66.7%), an observed gain of one task and 16.7 percentage points. The gain consists of b and f changing from failure to success, offset by c changing from success to failure. The other pairs are ties: a and e both pass, d fails twice. Keep the loss on c in the result (S1).

The executor clock moves in the unfavorable direction: 10+20+10+20+10+20 = 90 seconds without the method; 14+32+30+24+13+29 = 142 with Z. That is 52 extra seconds, not an observed speed saving. These clocks contain no billing or token data and leave preparation, review and correction unmeasured. They cannot establish monetary savings or be translated into bills (S1).

The blog's forty-point lift cannot supply the missing method attribution. It compares different models, Small without Z and Large with Z, and its Z denominator excludes three timeouts. Without raw task records and an equal-model arm, the contributions of model, method and exclusion cannot be separated (S2). The publication's "final" field is no independent confirmation either: it contains the same six tasks repeatedly examined to develop and select Z. That is exposed selection material (S1, S4).

There is also an outcome-label defect. Under S3's rule, an already committed action must never be repeated, and reconciliation must resolve commit state before retry. The baseline's reconciliation/no-prior-commit condition satisfies that rule, despite missing the preferred phrase; its rejection is false. The Z answer permits retry after every timeout, which can repeat a committed action; its acceptance is false even if a heading says "safe replay" (S3).

A minimal useful next comparison would freeze the current method and use one fixed model/client/effort/tools setting. First check the grader on independently labeled examples of the adopted requirement, including the two contrasting behaviors in S3; reward the outcome rule rather than a keyword. Then obtain genuinely new task groups unseen during method selection or grader tuning, run both arms on each task, and keep all outcomes, timeouts and regressions. Set the practical quality threshold in advance and record actual billing plus executor, preparation, review and correction effort. Use the new paired results and their uncertainty to decide whether to extend the study and whether a narrower release claim is warranted. def requirements(*statuses):
    return [{"id": f"C-{i}", "status": status, "evidence": "fixture observation"}
            for i, status in enumerate(statuses, 1)]


def minimal_evidence():
    blobs = {}

    def retain(text):
        sha = report.digest(text.encode())
        blobs[sha] = text
        return sha

    source_sha = report.digest(b"fixed cases")
    source = retain("source")
    trials, runs, grades, events = [], [], [], []
    pair = ["method-a", "method-b"]
    for case, arms in (("C-M", ("00", "10", "01", "11")), ("C-C", ("00", "11"))):
        for arm in arms:
            run_id = f"R{len(trials) + 1:02d}"
            skills = [pair[i] for i, enabled in enumerate(arm) if enabled == "1"]
            files = {"inputs/source.txt": source}
            files.update({f"skill/{name}/SKILL.md": retain(name) for name in skills})
            manifest = retain(json.dumps({"case_id": case, "source_sha256": source_sha, "files": files}))
            trials.append({"run_id": run_id, "case_id": case, "block": "C", "arm": arm,
                           "skills": skills, "packet_files": files,
                           "packet_manifest_sha256": manifest, "launch_sha256": retain("launch")})
            runs.append({"run_id": run_id, "case_id": case, "status": "completed",
                         "output_files": {"answer.md": retain("answer"), "source.txt": source},
                         "source_files": {"source.txt": source}, "changed_source_files": [], "new_files": ["answer.md"]})
            grades.append({"run_id": run_id, "case_id": case, "arm": arm,
                           "requirements": requirements("met", "not_verified")})
            events.extend({"run_id": run_id, "event": event} for event in ("spawn_observed", "completion_observed"))
    plan = {"trials": trials, "input_digests": {"comparison-cases.json": source_sha},
            "blocks": [{"id": "C", "main_case": "C-M", "control_case": "C-C", "skills": pair}]}
    evidence = {"runs": runs, "blobs": blobs, "execution_events": events}
    grades = {"runs": grades}
    rubric = {"cases": [{"id": case, "requirements": requirements("met", "met")} for case in ("C-M", "C-C")]}
    return plan, evidence, grades, rubric


def add_receipt(data, *, suite_status="met"):
    evidence = data[1]
    run = evidence["runs"][0]
    checker = report.digest(b"constructed checker")
    evidence["blobs"][checker] = "constructed checker"
    receipt = {"run_id": run["run_id"], "case": run["case_id"], "checker_sha256": checker,
               "subject_inventory_sha256": report.digest(json.dumps(run["output_files"], sort_keys=True).encode()),
               "evaluator_preserved_subject_bytes": True,
               "criteria": requirements("met", "not_verified"),
               "evidence": {"submitted_suite_assessment": {"status": suite_status}}}
    text = json.dumps(receipt)
    sha = report.digest(text.encode())
    evidence["blobs"][sha] = text
    evidence["deterministic_receipts"] = {run["run_id"]: {"v2_blob_sha256": sha}}
    return receipt, sha

# Evidence decision for Method Z

Do not ship Z under the claim that it is a proven quality and cost improvement. S1 is exposed exploratory evidence, S2 does not isolate the method, S3 contains grading errors, and S4 overstates these records. A population quality gain, cross-model generalization and monetary savings remain unestablished (S1-S4).

| S1 arm | Successes | Executor time |
|---|---:|---:|
| No method | 3/6 = 50.0% | 90 seconds |
| Z | 4/6 = 66.7% | 142 seconds |

The observed difference is +1 successful task, or +16.7 percentage points. Tasks b and f improve from 0 to 1, while c regresses from 1 to 0. Tasks a and e succeed in both arms; d fails in both. Z adds 52 executor seconds, about 57.8%, so this sample shows no speed saving. Executor time excludes billing, tokens, preparation, review and correction; monetary cost is unresolved (S1).

## Record reconciliation

S2's 40% to 80% comparison changes Small/no method to Large/Z and drops three timed-out Z runs. The model change and unequal denominator prevent attributing the reported +40 percentage points to Z alone. Raw paired data and an equal-model comparison are unavailable (S2).

The adopted requirement in S3 is to avoid repeating a committed action and settle commit state by reconciliation first. The baseline requires reconciliation to prove no prior commit, so rejecting it for lacking "safe replay" is a false rejection. "Always retry after timeout" can repeat an already committed action, so rewarding the Z answer's heading is a false acceptance. Both labels must be corrected by meaning, not phrase presence (S3).

Freeze Z and calibrate outcome grading against the adopted contract, including a reconciliation-first valid answer and an unconditional-retry invalid answer (S3). In one fixed client/model/effort/tool configuration, compare no method and Z on the same genuinely new task groups kept out of development and grader calibration. Randomize paired run order, retain every task and timeout, and report paired improvements and regressions. Measure executor time and actual billing, preparation, review and correction separately (S1, S2). Prespecify the quality gain and cost evidence needed for release; the supplied records do not justify an exact confirmatory sample size. Expand the new matched study if uncertainty remains. This is proposed work, and these records establish neither benefit in the population nor equivalence (S1-S4).
